devdoc.details: This contract implements a proxy that is upgradeable by an admin. To avoid https://medium.com/nomic-labs-blog/malicious-backdoors-in-ethereum-proxies-62629adf3357[proxy selector clashing], which can potentially be used in an attack, this contract uses the https://blog.openzeppelin.com/the-transparent-proxy-pattern/[transparent proxy pattern]. This pattern implies two things that go hand in hand: 1. If any account other than the admin calls the proxy, the call will be forwarded to the implementation, even if that call matches one of the admin functions exposed by the proxy itself. 2. If the admin calls the proxy, it can access the admin functions, but its calls will never be forwarded to the implementation. If the admin tries to call a function on the implementation it will fail with an error that says "admin cannot fallback to proxy target". These properties mean that the admin account can only be used for admin actions like upgrading the proxy or changing the admin, so it's best if it's a dedicated account that is not used for anything else. This will avoid headaches due to sudden errors when trying to call a function from the proxy implementation. Our recommendation is for the dedicated account to be an instance of the {ProxyAdmin} contract. If set up this way, you should think of the `ProxyAdmin` instance as the real administrative interface of your proxy. NOTE: The real interface of this proxy is that defined in `ITransparentUpgradeableProxy`. This contract does not inherit from that interface, and instead the admin functions are implicitly implemented using a custom dispatch mechanism in `_fallback`. Consequently, the compiler will not produce an ABI for this contract. This is necessary to fully implement transparency without decoding reverts caused by selector clashes between the proxy and the implementation. WARNING: It is not recommended to extend this contract to add additional external functions. If you do so, the compiler will not check that there are no selector conflicts, due to the note above. A selector clash between any new function and the functions declared in {ITransparentUpgradeableProxy} will be resolved in favor of the new one. This could render the admin operations inaccessible, which could prevent upgradeability. Transparency may also be compromised.

constructor.details: Initializes an upgradeable proxy managed by `_admin`, backed by the implementation at `_logic`, and optionally initialized with `_data` as explained in {ERC1967Proxy-constructor}.

activateNodeOperator(uint256).details: only accept call from address having `MANAGER` role

params._operatorId: Id of the operator to activate

addValidatorKeys(bytes[],bytes[],bytes[].details: only accepts call from onboarded NOs along with sufficient SD lockup

params._depositSignature: signature of a validator for 31ETH deposit
params._preDepositSignature: signature of a validators for 1ETH deposit

allocateValidatorsAndUpdateOperatorId(ui.details: first iteration is round robin based on capacity, second iteration exhaust the capacity in sequential manner and update the operatorId to pick operator for next sequence in next cycle all array start with index 1

params._numValidators: validator to deposit with permissioned pool

returns.selectedOperatorCapacity: operator wise count of validator to deposit

confirmRewardAddressChange(address).details: only the new reward address (msg.sender) can confirm

deactivateNodeOperator(uint256).details: only accept call from address having `MANAGER` role

params._operatorId: Id of the operator to deactivate

params._pageNumber: The page number of the results to fetch (starting from 1).
params._pageSize: The maximum number of items per page.

returns._0: An array of `Validator` objects representing the active validators.

getOperatorTotalKeys(uint256).details: length of the validatorIds array for an operator

params._endIndex: up to end index of validator queue to to count
params._nodeOperator: @notice operator total non terminal keys within a specified validator list
params._startIndex: start index in validator queue to start with

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

getTotalQueuedValidatorCount().details: compute by looping over operators queued keys count

params._pageNumber: The page number of the results to fetch (starting from 1).
params._pageSize: The maximum number of items per page.

returns._0: An array of `Validator` objects representing all validators for an operator

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

increaseTotalActiveValidatorCount(uint25.details: only permissioned pool calls it when it does the deposit of 1 ETH for validator

params._count: count to increase total active validator value

markValidatorReadyToDeposit(bytes[],byte.details: only stader oracle contract can call

params._frontRunPubkey: array for pubkeys which got front deposit
params._invalidSignaturePubkey: array of pubkey which has invalid signature for deposit
params._readyToDepositPubkey: array of pubkeys ready to be moved to DEPOSIT state

params._operatorRewardAddress: eth1 address of operator to get rewards and withdrawals

returns.feeRecipientAddress: fee recipient address for all validator clients of a operator

pause().details: Triggers stopped state. Contract must not be paused

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

proposeRewardAddress(address,address).details: only the existing reward address (msg.sender) can propose

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

unpause().details: Returns to normal state. Contract must be paused

params._inputKeyCountLimit: updated maximum key limit in the input

params._maxOperatorId: value of new max operator Id

params._nextQueuedValidatorIndex: updated next index of queued validator per operator

params._verifiedKeysBatchSize: updated maximum verified key limit in the oracle input

whitelistPermissionedNOs(address[]).details: only `MANAGER` can call, whitelisting a one way change there is no blacklisting

withdrawnValidators(bytes[]).details: list of pubkeys reported by oracle, revert if terminal validators are reported

activateNodeOperator(uint256).notice: activate a node operator for running new validator clients

confirmRewardAddressChange(address).notice: confirms and sets the new reward address of an operator

deactivateNodeOperator(uint256).notice: deactivate a node operator from running new validator clients

getAllActiveValidators(uint256,uint256).notice: Returns an array of active validators

getOperatorTotalKeys(uint256).notice: get the total added keys for an operator

getTotalActiveValidatorCount().notice: returns total active keys for permissioned pool

getTotalQueuedValidatorCount().notice: computes total queued keys for permissioned pool

getValidatorsByOperator(address,uint256,.notice: Returns an array of all validators for an Operator

increaseTotalActiveValidatorCount(uint25.notice: increase the total active validator count

markValidatorReadyToDeposit(bytes[],byte.notice: move validator state from PRE_DEPOSIT to DEPOSIT after verifying pre-sign message, front running and deposit signature. report front run and invalid signature pubkeys

markValidatorStatusAsPreDeposit(bytes).notice: update the status of a validator to `PRE_DEPOSIT`

proposeRewardAddress(address,address).notice: propose the new reward address of an operator

updateDepositStatusAndBlock(uint256).notice: sets the deposit block for a validator and update status to DEPOSITED

updateInputKeyCountLimit(uint16).notice: update number of validator keys that can be added in a single tx by the operator

updateMaxOperatorId(uint256).notice: update the max operator Id value

updateOperatorName(string).notice: update the name of an operator

updateVerifiedKeysBatchSize(uint256).notice: update the max number of verified validator keys reported by oracle in single tx

whitelistPermissionedNOs(address[]).notice: white list the permissioned node operator

withdrawnValidators(bytes[]).notice: Flag fully withdrawn validators as reported by oracle.
